title: The salah clock
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Salah and praying in congregation
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y4 lesson 20 (Pupil PDF worksheet: the salah clock)
intro: Lesson 20: The gift of salah: times, wudu and qiblah. To understand why salah is a gift from Allah and what must be ready before we pray: the time, wudu and the qiblah

questions.q: Explain why we must pray each salah at its time.
questions.a: Allah made salah due at set times (4:103), so we pray when the time comes, not whenever we like.
questions.model: Point: each salah has its time. Evidence: 'prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times' (an-Nisa' 4:103). Explain: so we stop what we are doing when the time comes.

questions.q: The qiblah is the direction of ...
On the pupil PDF, fill in the salah clock: write each prayer's name beside its time of day and one thing you need ready before it.
questions.a: Fajr dawn, Dhuhr midday, Asr afternoon, Maghrib sunset, Isha night; wudu, clean place, qiblah
questions.model: Teacher writes Fajr at dawn: 'I need wudu and to face the qiblah.'

questions.q: use a compass app with a parent to find the qiblah at home; which direction is it from the UK?
why do Muslims all over the world face one qiblah?
questions.a: It unites the ummah in worship of Allah alone

questions.q: How many daily prayers are there?
Back to our ponder: how do we get ready for salah?
questions.a: Wudu, clean clothes and place, at the right time, facing the qiblah
